items.author: TOI WORLD DESK
items.description: Two sexual assault survivors in Scotland have launched CourtRobe, a campaign to help women feel more confident when giving evidence in court. Sarah Lee, 39, and Kayla Poulton, 36, are seeking clothing donations and shopping vouchers from department stores. The initiative, being developed with the University of Glasgow's Emma Ritch Law Clinic, also aims to provide free personal shopping sessions with trauma-trained retail staff.

items.description: A Texas grandfather who gained custody of his three grandchildren after their father's death in 2017 has won a legal battle against their mother over unpaid child support and medical expenses. The mother had challenged the payments, arguing that the grandfather had not provided sufficient documentation to support his claims.

items.title: Atlantic dye test shows 140 times more mixing within surface than across base
items.author: TOI SCIENCE DESK
items.description: In a recent experiment near Martha’s Vineyard, scientists introduced rhodamine dye into the Atlantic Ocean to study its behavior. The dye spread quickly in the surface waters but demonstrated a slower descent into deeper layers. Findings showed a marked difference in mixing rates, emphasizing the complexities of ocean stratification on substance movement. This research is vital for the advancement of nutrient and pollutant transport models.

items.author: YUDHVIR RANA
items.description: Teerath Singh was shot dead outside a gurdwara in Cheete Kalan village while his friend sustained injuries. Preliminary investigations indicate the murder was connected to an old land dispute rather than political rivalry. Police have identified four suspects and filed an FIR, but no arrests have been made yet.

items.title: Fake seizures, attack on prison guards: How 17 inmates escaped TN jail at midnight
items.author: RAM SUNDARAM
items.description: Seventeen undertrial inmates managed to escape from Thekkampatti sub-jail in Tamil Nadu's Theni district. They faked epileptic seizures to lure prison personnel into opening their cell. Once the guards entered, the inmates attacked them and fled the facility. Four of the escapees have been apprehended while thirteen remain at large despite extensive police efforts. Investigations into the jailbreak and security lapses at the jail are currently ongoing.

items.description: New research highlights that individuals frequently misjudge how much others enjoy their company during interactions. items.title: Feral cat control helps NZ dotterel population rise from 105 to 160
items.author: TOI WORLD DESK
items.description: New Zealand's critically endangered southern dotterel population has risen by 52 percent following focused predator control efforts. Intensive campaigns targeting feral cats on Stewart Island have yielded immediate gains in breeding. The population grew from 105 birds in early 2025 to an estimated 160 in April 2026. Wildlife officials stress that ongoing management of feral cats is crucial for the bird's long-term survival.

items.title: Jio IPO delivers smaller payday for bankers than other mega offerings
items.description: In a landmark move, Jio Platforms, supported by Mukesh Ambani, successfully secured ₹30,213 crore, marking the largest IPO in India’s history. Investment bankers were rewarded with ₹196 crore in fees, translating to only 0.65% of the total amount raised. In contrast, Hyundai Motor India achieved ₹27,859 crore while paying out a heftier ₹493 crore in fees, which amount to 1.77%.

items.title: Indian markets rebound, but rising oil prices keep investors cautious
items.description: On Monday, Indian equity markets staged a comeback following four days of losses, with both the BSE Sensex and NSE Nifty seeing notable gains as investors sought to take advantage of cheaper stock prices. However, analysts warn that this recovery is precarious, influenced by global geopolitical issues and high crude oil prices.

items.title: Retail investors return to equities with Rs 10,572 crore buying in September
items.description: After two months of silence, September marked the return of retail investors to the secondary market, as they invested ₹10,572 crore in equities. This shift occurred after a significant market dip linked to escalating oil prices. In contrast, foreign portfolio investors continued their exit strategy. Additionally, the primary market thrived with ₹5,650 crore in shares bought by retail investors, emphasizing that upcoming market conditions will shape their future involvement.

items.title: Rising concentration in AI stocks poses a risk: Kunal Kapoor, Morningstar CEO
items.description: Kunal Kapoor, the CEO of Morningstar, voiced unease about the dangers of focusing investments heavily on AI stocks during his Mumbai trip. He stressed that lofty expectations might not always reflect in company profits, potentially leading to disappointing market outcomes. While praising India's compelling growth story, he remarked that its investment valuations do not stand up favorably against those in emerging markets.

items.author: TOI WORLD DESK
items.description: A man who bought a box of 22 old medals for just £25 at a car-boot sale in West Yorkshire discovered that one was a rare 18th-century medal commemorating Captain James Cook's death in 1779. After selling the other medals for £500, he took the rare piece to an auction house, where it later fetched £5,000. The medal was purchased by the Captain Cook Memorial Museum in Whitby for a special exhibition planned for 2028.
